race.name: Granfondo Tre Valli Varesine
race.tagline: A 126 km UCI qualifier and 2026 European Championship course with 1,993m of climbing through the Italian pre-Alps

vitals.field_size: No participant cap is stated in the current official regulations
vitals.start_format: Age-category waves start every five minutes from 9:00am; the published start window is 9:00-9:40am from Via Luigi Sacco 5
vitals.registration: Online registration includes the race pack, timing chip, on-course support, refreshments, pasta party, showers, and bike storage; a one-day FCI license is required for riders without an accepted racing license. The first 25% of finishers in each UCI age category qualify for the 2027 UCI Gran Fondo World Championships
vitals.entry_fee: €60 online from August 3 through October 1; €80 on site, plus €10 for the FCI one-day license when required
vitals.feed_zones: Gran Fondo refreshments at approximately km 37.2 (Cugliate Fabiasco), km 64.6 (Brezzo di Bedero), km 88.5 (Castello Cabiaglio), and km 125.0 in Varese; the final stop includes a gluten-free option
vitals.cutoff_time: Reach the Gran Fondo/Medio Fondo split at Bosco, Montegrino Valtravaglia by 12:00pm or continue on the shorter Medio Fondo route; riders passed by the end-of-race vehicle continue under normal traffic rules
route_options: 100 km (Medio Fondo): 1,447m elevation in the regulations; qualifier for men 60+ and women 50+
126 km (Gran Fondo): 1,993m elevation in the regulations; qualifier for men 19-59 and women 19-49

climate.primary: Cool fall weather with variable conditions
climate.description: Early October in Lombardy brings mild autumn conditions with cool mornings and potential afternoon warmth. The proximity to three lakes (Lugano, Maggiore, Varese) moderates temperatures but increases rain risk. Riders should prepare for variable conditions ranging from crisp mornings to mild afternoons with possible precipitation.

terrain.primary: Hilly pre-alpine terrain with significant climbing on fully paved roads
terrain.surface: A fully paved road course with sustained climbs, narrow passages, tunnels, and several descents the official time schedule marks as demanding. Traffic is temporarily controlled around the race convoy, but the regulations do not promise closure for the entire event; riders passed by the end-of-race vehicle must follow normal road rules.
features: Alpe Tedesco via SP29 early in the race
Ardena to the Santuario della Madonna di Ardena
Gran Fondo-only Lake Maggiore loop through Luino, Germignaga, Brezzo di Bedero, Porto Valtravaglia, and Castelveccana
technical descents and narrow bridge sections identified in the official time schedule
rolling return through Brinzio, Castello Cabiaglio, Orino, and the Lake Varese shoreline
final rise from Schiranna to Via Sacco in central Varese

climb_profile.profile_type: Repeated pre-alpine climbs with technical descents and a rising finish

course_description.character: The regulation distance is 126 km with 1,993 m of climbing, although the August race-guide summary rounds that to 127 km and 1,990 m. The Gran Fondo starts and finishes on Via Sacco in central Varese, crosses Alpe Tedesco and Ardena, takes the long Lake Maggiore loop, then returns through the Valcuvia hills and along Lake Varese before the final rise into town.
course_description.signature_challenge: The climbing is cumulative and the protection clock matters: Alpe Tedesco and Ardena arrive early, the Gran Fondo extension adds the Lake Maggiore and Roggiano terrain, and riders must reach the Montegrino Valtravaglia split by noon to stay on the long course.
suffering_zones: Lake Maggiore Extension and Brezzo di Bedero
Valcuvia Hills and the Varese Return

logistics.airport: The official guide identifies Milano Malpensa and Milano Linate as the nearest airports, with train or rental-car connections onward to Varese.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Base in Varese if you want the simplest race morning: bib pickup, the Race Village, start, finish, bike storage, and pasta party are centered on the Giardini Estensi and Via Sacco 5.
logistics.transport: Varese is served by rail and by the A8/A9 motorway network. The organizer says the station is close enough to reach the event area by bike or taxi and lists parking near the event area.
logistics.food: The pasta party begins at noon at the Giardini Estensi. Four Gran Fondo refreshment points are shown in the official time schedule, with green waste zones at each and a gluten-free option at the final stop.

history.origin_story: SC Alfredo Binda launched the amateur Granfondo Tre Valli Varesine in 2016 alongside the region's long-running professional race. Varese hosted the UCI Gran Fondo World Championships on this terrain in 2018, and the current organizer describes the 2026 event as the tenth edition on the Worlds route. The October 4 Gran Fondo is both a UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier for the 2027 Worlds and the road race for the 2026 UEC Granfondo European Championships.
notable_moments: Founded in 2016 as an amateur companion to the historic professional Tre Valli Varesine
Hosted 2018 UCI Gran Fondo World Championships in Varese
Serves as a UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier for the 2027 World Championships
Hosts the UEC Granfondo European Championships on October 3-4, 2026
The organizer calls 2026 the tenth edition
history.reputation: Granfondo Tre Valli Varesine carries unusual amateur-racing weight through its UCI qualifier status, 2018 Worlds history, and 2026 UEC championship role. SC Alfredo Binda links the mass-participation race to Varese's professional cycling tradition.

biased_opinion.verdict: Prestige-driven UCI qualifier with legitimate teeth
biased_opinion.summary: Granfondo Tre Valli Varesine trades on genuine cycling heritage and UCI credentials. The 126 km course with 1,993 m of climbing delivers a real pre-alpine test, and its 2026 UEC championship status raises the competitive stakes. The key practical detail is the noon split at Montegrino Valtravaglia: miss it and the organizer directs you onto the Medio Fondo.
strengths: UCI World Series qualifier with World Championships pedigree
Legitimate 126 km course with 1,993m climbing on technical terrain
Race-convoy road protection through scenic pre-alpine and lake regions
Gran Fondo and Medio Fondo options at 126 km and 100 km
weaknesses: Road closure ends when the end-of-race vehicle passes
The noon route-split gate can force slower riders onto the Medio Fondo
Age-category start waves spread across a 40-minute window
European Championship eligibility and UCI qualification rules require careful category checking
biased_opinion.bottom_line: This is a legitimate championship-level gran fondo with clear 2026 pricing and logistics. Race it for the UCI qualification opportunity, the UEC championship atmosphere, and the Varese setting; arrive trained to clear the noon split and handle technical descents after repeated climbs.

final_verdict.one_liner: A 126 km UCI qualifier and 2026 European Championship race where repeated climbs, technical descents, and a noon long-course gate reward disciplined preparation.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race this if you're targeting the 2027 UCI Gran Fondo World Championships, eligible for the 2026 UEC titles, or want a competitive Italian gran fondo on the Varese Worlds terrain. Skip if you want a relaxed open-road tour: the event is timed, category-started, and the long route has a firm noon split.
final_verdict.alternatives: For another Italian UCI qualifier, compare Granfondo Matildica. For a longer mass-participation Italian classic, compare Nove Colli; for a late-season Lombardy climbing event, compare Gran Fondo Il Lombardia.
